claim: Intracellular pH (pHi) dynamics is increasingly recognized as an important regulator of a range of normal and pathological cell behaviors.
source: Intracellular pH (pHi) dynamics is increasingly recognized as an important regulator of a range of normal and pathological cell behaviors.
evidence: This is a general statement about the field's recognition of pHi importance, drawing from established scientific consensus.

claim: Increased pHi is a conserved characteristic of cancers.
source: Notably, increased pHi is now acknowledged as a conserved characteristic of cancers
evidence: This statement reflects established scientific consensus about cancer cell pH characteristics.

claim: Increased pHi in cell models increases proliferation and migration as well as limits apoptosis.
source: in cell models is confirmed to increase proliferation and migration as well as limit apoptosis.
evidence: This statement refers to established findings from cell model studies.

claim: Increased pHi is sufficient to induce dysplasia in the absence of other transforming cues in Drosophila melanogaster.
source: Using Drosophila melanogaster, we show that increased pHi is sufficient to induce dysplasia in the absence of other transforming cues
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Increased pHi potentiates growth and invasion with oncogenic Ras in Drosophila.
source: we show that increased pHi is sufficient to induce dysplasia in the absence of other transforming cues and potentiates growth and invasion with oncogenic Ras.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data in the manuscript.

claim: Increased pHi was confirmed in situ using a genetically encoded biosensor.
source: Using a genetically encoded biosensor we also confirm increased pHi in situ.
evidence: This refers to experimental measurements using the mCherry-pHluorin biosensor.

claim: Limiting H+ efflux with oncogenic Raf or Ras induces acidosis and synthetic lethality in Drosophila models and clonal human mammary cells.
source: Moreover, in Drosophila models and clonal human mammary cells we show that limiting H+ efflux with oncogenic Raf or Ras induces acidosis and synthetic lethality.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data in both Drosophila and human cell models.

claim: Inhibiting H+ efflux causes lethality in invasive primary tumor cell lines.
source: Further, we show lethality in invasive primary tumor cell lines with inhibiting H+ efflux.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data with SW620 and MDA-MB-231 cell lines.

claim: Cancer cells have a lower extracellular pH (pHe) and higher intracellular pH (pHi) than normal cells.
source: Dysregulated pH is a common characteristic of cancer cells, which have a lower extracellular pH (pHe) and higher intracellular pH (pHi) than normal cells.
evidence: This statement reflects established scientific knowledge about cancer cell pH characteristics.

claim: The lower pHe of tumors is confirmed by pH-sensitive PET radiotracers, MR spectroscopy and MRI.
source: The lower pHe of tumors, confirmed by pH-sensitive PET radiotracers, MR spectroscopy and MRI (Zhang et al., 2010)
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Zhang et al., 2010.

claim: Lower pHe contributes to local metastatic invasion.
source: The lower pHe of tumors, confirmed by pH-sensitive PET radiotracers, MR spectroscopy and MRI (Zhang et al., 2010), contributes to local metastatic invasion (Cardone et al., 2005; Rofstad et al., 2006; Stock et al., 2008; Stock and Schwab, 2009; Busco et al., 2010; Estrella et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations.

claim: Increased pHi promotes cell proliferation.
source: Increased pHi enables a number of cancer cell behaviors, including promoting cell proliferation (Pouysségur et al., 1982; Kapus et al., 1994; Putney and Barber, 2003)
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Increased pHi promotes glycolytic metabolism.
source: Increased pHi enables a number of cancer cell behaviors, including promoting cell proliferation (Pouysségur et al., 1982; Kapus et al., 1994; Putney and Barber, 2003), glycolytic metabolism (Reshkin et al., 2000; Dietl et al., 2010; Webb et al., 2011)
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Increased pHi promotes migration.
source: Increased pHi enables a number of cancer cell behaviors, including promoting cell proliferation (Pouysségur et al., 1982; Kapus et al., 1994; Putney and Barber, 2003), glycolytic metabolism (Reshkin et al., 2000; Dietl et al., 2010; Webb et al., 2011), migration (Denker and Barber, 2002; Patel and Barber, 2005; Frantz et al., 2008; Stock and Schwab, 2009)
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Increased pHi promotes invasion.
source: Increased pHi enables a number of cancer cell behaviors, including promoting cell proliferation (Pouysségur et al., 1982; Kapus et al., 1994; Putney and Barber, 2003), glycolytic metabolism (Reshkin et al., 2000; Dietl et al., 2010; Webb et al., 2011), migration (Denker and Barber, 2002; Patel and Barber, 2005; Frantz et al., 2008; Stock and Schwab, 2009), and invasion (Reshkin et al., 2000; Hinton et al., 2009)
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Increased pHi limits apoptosis.
source: Increased pHi enables a number of cancer cell behaviors, including promoting cell proliferation (Pouysségur et al., 1982; Kapus et al., 1994; Putney and Barber, 2003), glycolytic metabolism (Reshkin et al., 2000; Dietl et al., 2010; Webb et al., 2011), migration (Denker and Barber, 2002; Patel and Barber, 2005; Frantz et al., 2008; Stock and Schwab, 2009), and invasion (Reshkin et al., 2000; Hinton et al., 2009), as well as limiting apoptosis (Matsuyama et al., 2000; Lagadic-Gossmann et al., 2004).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The higher pHi of cancer cells is paradoxical because increased production of metabolic acids from aerobic glycolysis would be predicted to lower pHi.
source: The higher pHi of cancer cells is paradoxical because increased production of metabolic acids generated by aerobic glycolysis would be predicted to lower pHi.
evidence: This is a logical inference based on metabolic principles.

claim: Many cancers have elevated expression or activity of carbonic anhydrase 9.
source: However, many cancers have elevated expression or activity of proteins that facilitate increased pHi, including carbonic anhydrase 9 (Swietach et al., 2007)
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Swietach et al., 2007.

claim: Many cancers have elevated expression or activity of H+-ATPases.
source: However, many cancers have elevated expression or activity of proteins that facilitate increased pHi, including carbonic anhydrase 9 (Swietach et al., 2007), H+-ATPases (Martinez-Zaguilan et al., 1993; Sennoune et al., 2004; Hinton et al., 2009)
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Many cancers have elevated expression or activity of the Na+-H+ exchanger NHE1.
source: However, many cancers have elevated expression or activity of proteins that facilitate increased pHi, including carbonic anhydrase 9 (Swietach et al., 2007), H+-ATPases (Martinez-Zaguilan et al., 1993; Sennoune et al., 2004; Hinton et al., 2009), the ubiquitously expressed Na+-H+ exchanger NHE1 (McLean et al., 2000; Miraglia et al., 2005; Chiang et al., 2008; Yang et al., 2011)
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Many cancers have elevated expression or activity of monocarboxylate transporter family members MCT1 and MCT4.
source: However, many cancers have elevated expression or activity of proteins that facilitate increased pHi, including carbonic anhydrase 9 (Swietach et al., 2007), H+-ATPases (Martinez-Zaguilan et al., 1993; Sennoune et al., 2004; Hinton et al., 2009), the ubiquitously expressed Na+-H+ exchanger NHE1 (McLean et al., 2000; Miraglia et al., 2005; Chiang et al., 2008; Yang et al., 2011) and the monocarboxylate transporter family members MCT1 and MCT4 (Pinheiro et al., 2010; Halestrap, 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Xenograft tumor growth is suppressed by inhibiting NHE1.
source: Xenograft tumor growth is suppressed by inhibiting NHE1 (Lagarde et al., 1988; Yang et al., 2011)
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Xenograft tumor growth is suppressed by inhibiting MCT1 activity.
source: Xenograft tumor growth is suppressed by inhibiting NHE1 (Lagarde et al., 1988; Yang et al., 2011) or MCT1 (Sonveaux et al., 2008; Colen et al., 2011) activity.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Inhibiting NHE1 activity reduces viability of breast cancer cells.
source: In cell models, inhibiting NHE1 activity reduces viability of breast cancer (Reshkin et al., 2003) and leukemic cells (Rich et al., 2000; Reshkin et al., 2003)
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Inhibiting NHE1 activity reduces viability of leukemic cells.
source: In cell models, inhibiting NHE1 activity reduces viability of breast cancer (Reshkin et al., 2003) and leukemic cells (Rich et al., 2000; Reshkin et al., 2003)
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Silencing MCT4 expression with RNA interference decreases survival of renal carcinoma cells.
source: silencing MCT4 expression with RNA interference decreases survival of renal carcinoma cells (Gerlinger et al., 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Gerlinger et al., 2012.

claim: Three NHE isoforms have been identified in Drosophila (Dnhe1-3).
source: Three NHE isoforms have been identified in Drosophila (Dnhe1-3)
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about Drosophila NHE isoforms.

claim: DmNhe2 is most homologous to mammalian plasma membrane NHE1 based on sequence analysis of C-terminal cytoplasmic domains.
source: sequence analysis of the C-terminal cytoplasmic domains suggests DmNhe2 is most homologous to the mammalian plasma membrane NHE1, one of nine mammalian isoforms (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is supported by sequence analysis data presented in Figure 1A.

claim: DmNhe2 contains a lysine/arginine-rich region (KR motif) in the juxtamembrane segment that binds phosphatidylinositol 4,5-bisphosphate in the plasma membrane.
source: Conserved features include a lysine/arginine-rich region (KR motif) in the juxtamembrane segment that binds phosphatidylinositol 4,5-bisphosphate in the plasma membrane (Putney and Barber, 2003)
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Putney and Barber, 2003.

claim: DmNhe2 contains a conserved binding motif for the calcineurin homologous protein CHP.
source: Conserved features include a lysine/arginine-rich region (KR motif) in the juxtamembrane segment that binds phosphatidylinositol 4,5-bisphosphate in the plasma membrane (Putney and Barber, 2003), a conserved binding motif for the calcineurin homologous protein CHP (Lin and Barber, 1996; Pang et al., 2001)
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: DmNhe2 contains a glutamic acid residue in the transmembrane domain that is essential for H+ efflux (E358 in DmNhe2 and E266 in human NHE1).
source: a glutamic acid residue in the transmembrane domain that is essential for H+ efflux (E358 in DmNhe2 and E266 in human NHE1)
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about NHE structure-function relationships.

claim: DmNhe2 contains consensus sites for phosphorylation by Akt and ATM/ATR kinases.
source: a glutamic acid residue in the transmembrane domain that is essential for H+ efflux (E358 in DmNhe2 and E266 in human NHE1) and consensus sites for phosphorylation by Akt and ATM/ATR kinases (Figure 1A, and Figure 1—figure supplements 1, 2).
evidence: This is supported by sequence analysis data presented in Figure 1A and supplementary figures.

claim: DmNhe2 has a role in charge-dependent plasma membrane recruitment of Dishevelled to establish planar cell polarity.
source: The only previous report on DmNhe2 function indicates a role in charge-dependent plasma membrane recruitment of Dishevelled to establish planar cell polarity (Simons et al., 2009).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Simons et al., 2009.

claim: GMR > Dnhe2 expression induced an externally rough adult eye with phenotypes consistent with dysplasia in the underlying epithelium.
source: GMR > Dnhe2 expression induced an externally rough adult eye with phenotypes consistent with dysplasia in the underlying epithelium (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: In GMR > Dnhe2 flies, ommatidial organization was disrupted and individual facets were irregular in shape and size.
source: In GMR > Dnhe2 flies, ommatidial organization was disrupted and individual facets were irregular in shape and size (Figure 1B,C, middle).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figures 1B and 1C.

claim: GMR > Dnhe2 retinae had misoriented ommatidia, abnormal cell fates and missing R cells.
source: In section, GMR > Dnhe2 retinae had misoriented ommatidia, abnormal cell fates and missing R cells (Figure 1D,E, middle).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figures 1D and 1E.

claim: GMR > Dnhe2E358I retinae had subtle defects in patterning, including rare bristle placement defects.
source: Externally, GMR > Dnhe2E358I retinae had subtle defects in patterning, including rare bristle placement defects (Figure 1B,C, right).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figures 1B and 1C.

claim: No patterning defects were evident in GMR > Dnhe2E358I retinae in section.
source: In section, no patterning defects were evident (Figure 1D,E, right)
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figures 1D and 1E.

claim: Dysplasia in GMR > Dnhe2 eyes is dependent on ion transport.
source: suggesting that dysplasia in GMR > Dnhe2 eyes is dependent on ion transport.
evidence: This is an inference based on the comparison between Dnhe2 and Dnhe2E358I phenotypes.

claim: There was no detectable difference in pHi between wild type and GMR > Dnhe2 in wL3 eye imaginal discs after ~24 hr of transgene expression.
source: After ∼24 hr of transgene expression there was no detectable difference in pHi between wild type and GMR > Dnhe2 in wL3 eye imaginal discs (data not shown).
evidence: This is a primary finding from experimental measurements.

claim: In pupal eyes at 42 hr after puparium formation, pHi in GMR > Dnhe2 was significantly higher than wild type in apical non-neural cells.
source: However, in pupal eyes at 42 hr after puparium formation (42H apf), pHi in GMR > Dnhe2 was significantly higher than wild type in both apical non-neural cells (Figure 1F,G)
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figures 1F and 1G.

claim: In pupal eyes at 42 hr after puparium formation, pHi in GMR > Dnhe2 was significantly higher than wild type in photoreceptor neurons.
source: However, in pupal eyes at 42 hr after puparium formation (42H apf), pHi in GMR > Dnhe2 was significantly higher than wild type in both apical non-neural cells (Figure 1F,G) and in photoreceptor neurons (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: pHi in pupal eyes expressing GMR > Dnhe2E358I was not different than wild type.
source: In contrast, pHi in pupal eyes expressing the mutant GMR > Dnhe2E358I was not different than wild type (Figure 1F,G)
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figures 1F and 1G.

claim: The Dnhe2E358I mutant lacks H+ efflux.
source: In contrast, pHi in pupal eyes expressing the mutant GMR > Dnhe2E358I was not different than wild type (Figure 1F,G), indicating that this mutant lacks H+ efflux.
evidence: This is an inference based on the pHi measurements and the known function of the E358 residue.

claim: Patterning defects in GMR > Dnhe2 retinae reflect constitutively increased pHi.
source: These data suggest that patterning defects in GMR > Dnhe2 retinae reflect constitutively increased pHi
evidence: This is an inference based on the correlation between increased pHi and patterning defects.

claim: GMR > Dnhe2 pupal eyes had severely disrupted cell shapes and tissue organization.
source: GMR > Dnhe2 pupal eyes had severely disrupted cell shapes and tissue organization
evidence: This is a primary finding from histological analysis.

claim: Ommatidia in GMR > Dnhe2 pupal eyes were overall smaller than in wild type.
source: and ommatidia overall were smaller than in wild type.
evidence: This is a primary finding from histological analysis.

claim: GMR > Dnhe2 ommatidia had aberrant numbers of cone and primary pigment cells.
source: Ommatidia had aberrant numbers of cone and primary pigment cells (pink).
evidence: This is a primary finding from histological analysis.

claim: Some ommatidia in GMR > Dnhe2 pupal eyes were fused.
source: Some ommatidia were fused (red), reflecting fused lenses seen in adult eyes (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is a primary finding from histological analysis.

claim: Overall phalloidin levels were lower in GMR > Dnhe2 pupal retinae compared to wild type.
source: In GMR > Dnhe2 pupal retinae, overall phalloidin levels were lower
evidence: This is a primary finding from immunofluorescence analysis.

claim: The differences in phalloidin labeling between cell types were less pronounced in GMR > Dnhe2 pupal retinae.
source: and the differences between cell types were less pronounced.
evidence: This is a primary finding from immunofluorescence analysis.

claim: Increasing pHi in the developing eye causes profound defects in tissue architecture that affect all cell types.
source: From these data, increasing pHi in the developing eye causes profound defects in tissue architecture that affect all cell types in the developing Drosophila eye
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data on GMR > Dnhe2 phenotypes.

claim: Increasing pHi shows severe disruption of patterning throughout the multilayered epithelium of the Drosophila eye.
source: and shows severe disruption of patterning throughout this complex, multilayered epithelium.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data on GMR > Dnhe2 phenotypes.

claim: The phenotypes of increased pHi are consistent with dysplasia.
source: These phenotypes are consistent with dysplasia
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental findings.

claim: The phenotypes of increased pHi are similar to effects of expressing activated, oncogenic Raf.
source: and are similar to effects of expressing activated, oncogenic Raf, as shown below.
evidence: This is a comparison to data presented later in the manuscript.

claim: Cell proliferation was substantially increased with GMR > Dnhe2 expression.
source: Consistent with increased pHi being a conserved proliferative signal from yeasts (Orij et al., 2012) to mammals (Pouysségur et al., 1982; Kapus et al., 1994; Putney and Barber, 2003), cell proliferation was substantially increased with GMR > Dnhe2 expression.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data.

claim: With GMR > Dnhe2 expression, there was a significant increase in the number of proliferating phospho-histone H3 positive cells posterior to the second mitotic wave.
source: With GMR > Dnhe2 expression, we found a significant increase in the number of proliferating phospho-histone H3 (phosH3) positive cells within this posterior region (Figure 2C,D).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figures 2C and 2D.

claim: In en > GFP, Dnhe2 expressing wing discs, there was overgrowth and dysplasia only in the expressing compartment.
source: In en > GFP, Dnhe2 expressing wing discs, there was overgrowth and dysplasia only in the expressing compartment, while non-expressing tissue resembled wild type (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: With en > Dnhe2 expression, there were significantly more proliferating cells in the posterior compared with anterior compartment.
source: With en > Dnhe2 expression, however, this distribution was markedly different with significantly more proliferating cells in the posterior compared with anterior compartment (Figure 2F,G).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figures 2F and 2G.

claim: Dnhe2 acts in a cell-autonomous manner to promote proliferation and dysplasia.
source: Together, these data suggest that Dnhe2 acts in a cell-autonomous manner to promote proliferation and dysplasia.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data on compartment-specific expression.

claim: NHE1 activity promotes directed cell migration in cultured cells.
source: NHE1 activity promotes directed cell migration (Denker and Barber, 2002; Patel and Barber, 2005; Stock and Schwab, 2009) and invasion (Stock and Schwab, 2009; Busco et al., 2010) in cultured cells
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: NHE1 activity promotes invasion in cultured cells.
source: NHE1 activity promotes directed cell migration (Denker and Barber, 2002; Patel and Barber, 2005; Stock and Schwab, 2009) and invasion (Stock and Schwab, 2009; Busco et al., 2010) in cultured cells
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Expression of RasV12 induced a wider ptc > GFP stripe compared to control (~1.6-fold increase).
source: Expression of RasV12 induced a wider ptc > GFP stripe compared to control (∼1.6-fold increase)
evidence: This is a primary finding from experimental measurements.

claim: Expression of Dnhe2 alone did not increase the ptc > GFP stripe width.
source: while expression of Dnhe2 alone did not (Figure 3A–C).

claim: Co-expression of RasV12 and Dnhe2 markedly increased the ptc > GFP stripe width greater than twofold.
source: However, co-expression of RasV12 and Dnhe2 markedly increased the ptc > GFP stripe width greater than twofold (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: There was a significant increase in the overall size of the wing disc with ptc > RasV12, Dnhe2 compared with either transgene alone or wild type.
source: We also observed a significant increase in the overall size of the wing disc with ptc > RasV12, Dnhe2 compared with either transgene alone or wild type (Figure 3A,D).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figures 3A and 3D.

claim: In control and Dnhe2-expressing discs, only a single instance of a few single GFP-positive cells was found.
source: In control and Dnhe2-expressing discs we found only a single instance of a few (Rofstad et al., 2006; Stock and Schwab, 2009; Zhang et al., 2010) single GFP-positive cells
evidence: This is a primary finding from experimental observations.

claim: No examples of invasive cells were found in RasV12-expressing discs.
source: and no examples in RasV12-expressing discs (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: In ptc > RasV12, Dnhe2 discs, examples of invasive cells were found in all discs examined.
source: However, in ptc > RasV12, Dnhe2 discs, we found examples of invasive cells in all discs examined.
evidence: This is a primary finding from experimental observations.

claim: Several different types of invasive behaviors were found in ptc > RasV12, Dnhe2 discs, including basal expansion of the ptc stripe, single invasive cells and streams of cells migrating out of the stripe.
source: Further, we found several different types of invasive behaviors, including basal expansion of the ptc stripe, single invasive cells and streams of cells migrating out of the stripe into neighboring tissue in the posterior compartment (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: Dnhe2 expression has cell autonomous effects on growth and migration behaviors.
source: These data show cell autonomous effects of Dnhe2 expression on growth and migration behaviors
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data on ptc-driven expression.

claim: Dnhe2 expression has non-autonomous effects on tissue growth.
source: as well as non-autonomous effects on tissue growth.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data on overall wing disc size.

claim: Homozygous Dnhe2null flies had ~20% survival to eclosion.
source: Homozygous Dnhe2null flies had ∼20% survival to eclosion (Figure 4C)
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Surviving adult Dnhe2null flies appeared morphologically normal.
source: and surviving adult flies appeared morphologically normal.
evidence: This is a primary finding from experimental observations.

claim: The lethality of Dnhe2null flies was rescued by expression of Dnhe2 using the muscle-specific mef2-GAL4 driver.
source: The lethality of Dnhe2null flies was rescued by expression of Dnhe2 using the muscle-specific mef2-GAL4 driver, but not using the neuronal elav-GAL4 driver (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The lethality of Dnhe2null flies was not rescued by expression of Dnhe2 using the neuronal elav-GAL4 driver.
source: The lethality of Dnhe2null flies was rescued by expression of Dnhe2 using the muscle-specific mef2-GAL4 driver, but not using the neuronal elav-GAL4 driver (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Retinal architecture in homozygous Dnhe2null flies was organized and regular, resembling wild type.
source: Retinal architecture in homozygous Dnhe2null flies was organized and regular, resembling wild type (Figure 5A,B).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figures 5A and 5B.

claim: The external surface of GMR > Raf eyes was disorganized with indistinct facets and a rough exterior retinal surface.
source: The external surface of GMR > Raf eyes was disorganized with indistinct facets and a rough exterior retinal surface (Figure 5A,B).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figures 5A and 5B.

claim: Some ommatidia in GMR > Raf eyes showed thin or absent lenses.
source: Some ommatidia showed thin or absent lenses.
evidence: This is a primary finding from experimental observations.

claim: GMR > Raf eyes had ommatidial defects with mis-orientation and occasional missing rhabdomeres.
source: In section, GMR > Raf had ommatidial defects with mis-orientation and occasional missing rhabdomeres (Figure 5C, tracing in Figure 5D).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figures 5C and 5D.

claim: GMR > Raf rhabdomeres were morphologically distinct from wild type, appearing more rectangular, especially in R1, R3, R5 and R6.
source: Additionally, GMR > Raf rhabdomeres were morphologically distinct from wild type, appearing more rectangular, especially in R1, R3, R5 and R6.
evidence: This is a primary finding from histological analysis.

claim: Externally, Dnhe2null; GMR > Raf appeared identical to GMR > Raf, except that the eye color was noticeably lighter and yellowed.
source: Externally, Dnhe2null; GMR > Raf appeared identical to GMR > Raf (Figure 5A,B), except that the eye color was noticeably lighter and yellowed.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figures 5A and 5B.

claim: Tangential retinal sections of Dnhe2null; GMR > Raf revealed a complete loss of tissue architecture and cell structure, with histological features of coagulative necrosis.
source: Tangential retinal sections revealed a complete loss of tissue architecture and cell structure, with histological features of coagulative necrosis, including loss of rhabdomere morphology, absence of distinct cell membranes and diffusion of pigment granules (Figure 5C).

claim: Live, dissected whole-mount adult eyes of Dnhe2null; GMR > Raf revealed a significant reduction of the cohesive, red-pigmented retinal epithelial layer.
source: Live, dissected whole-mount adult eyes revealed a significant reduction of the cohesive, red-pigmented retinal epithelial layer, such that the remaining Dnhe2null; GMR > Raf tissue was thin and transparent in appearance (data not shown).
evidence: This is a primary finding from experimental observations.

claim: There is a synthetic lethal interaction between loss of Dnhe2 and expression of oncogenic Raf.
source: These observations support a synthetic lethal interaction between loss of Dnhe2 and expression of oncogenic Raf.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data on Dnhe2null; GMR > Raf phenotypes.

claim: Synthetic lethality of Dnhe2null; GMR > Raf was progressive.
source: Synthetic lethality of Dnhe2null; GMR > Raf was progressive, as determined by examining earlier developmental stages.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data at different developmental stages.

claim: In wL3 eye discs, Dnhe2null tissue morphology was indistinguishable from wild type.
source: In wL3 eye discs, Dnhe2null tissue morphology was indistinguishable from wild type (Figure 6A)
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: In wL3 eye discs, Dnhe2null tissue had fewer proliferating cells than wild type as indicated by phosH3 staining.
source: however there were fewer proliferating cells than in wild type as indicated by phosH3 staining (Figure 6A,B).

claim: Compared with GMR > Raf, the morphology of Dnhe2null; GMR > Raf appeared less disrupted in wL3 eye discs.
source: Compared with GMR > Raf the morphology of Dnhe2null; GMR > Raf appeared less disrupted (Figure 6A)

claim: Hyperproliferation was suppressed in Dnhe2null; GMR > Raf compared with GMR > Raf in wL3 eye discs.

claim: Cells in all genotypes retain their fates as differentiated neurons in pupal eyes at 42H apf as indicated by Elav expression.
source: Pupal eyes were assayed 42H apf for expression of the neuronal antigen Elav, and we found that cells in all genotypes retain their fates as differentiated neurons (Figure 6C).

claim: Dnhe2null pupal eyes appeared wild type with 4 cone cells and 2 primary pigment cells visible on the apical surface, and a single row of secondary pigment cells separating neighboring ommatidia.
source: Dnhe2null pupal eyes appeared wild type: individual ommatidia had 4 cone cells and 2 primary pigment cells visible on the apical surface, and a single row of secondary pigment cells separating neighboring ommatidia.

claim: Cell morphologies in Dnhe2null pupal eyes were slightly abnormal, with secondary pigment cells thicker than in wild type and irregular cell shapes and cell-cell contacts.
source: However, cell morphologies were slightly abnormal (Figure 6D,E). Secondary pigment cells were thicker than in wild type, and cell shapes and cell–cell contacts were irregular.

claim: With expression of GMR > Raf, cell morphologies in pupal eyes were profoundly aberrant, with extra and mis-shapen cone cells and ommatidia mis-aligned along the D/V axis.
source: With expression of GMR > Raf, cell morphologies were profoundly aberrant, with extra and mis-shapen cone cells and ommatidia mis-aligned along the D/V axis, as seen in adults.
evidence: This is a primary finding from histological analysis.

claim: In GMR > Raf pupal eyes, immature cone cell contacts were maintained and secondary pigment cells were absent between some pairs of neighboring ommatidia.
